answer: Divergent attestation binding. Each identity must lodge a signed, costly statement at a public wharf and later resolve it against a separate harbor checkpoint, so any clone fleet either reuses one statement and collides at audit or pays full issuance cost per copy. A shared pigment hash ties the record to the exact submission, making silent duplication detectable without extra verification rounds. The attacker's per-identity cost is the full attestation fee plus the loss of every bonded copy caught diverging.
